hypothesis: Player profile and stats endpoints on Pulselive work unauthenticated and can be parameterized by competitionId, seasonId, and playerId.
rationale: Network exploration shows high-interest endpoints /api/v1/players/{playerId} and /api/v2/competitions/8/seasons/2025/players/{playerId}/stats with multiple hits and no auth headers. We need to confirm they return JSON when accessed directly so we can build pl_player_profile_and_stats.
prompt:
You are exploring Premier League player APIs.
1. Use browser_navigate to https://www.premierleague.com/en/ and wait for load.
2. Use browser_navigate directly to https://sdp-prem-prod.premier-league-prod.pulselive.com/api/v1/players/1. After navigation, run browser_eval_js('document.body.innerText') and attempt JSON.parse in the page context. Report whether it is valid JSON and list Object.keys of the top-level object.
3. Then navigate to https://sdp-prem-prod.premier-league-prod.pulselive.com/api/v2/competitions/8/seasons/2025/players/1/stats and repeat the same capture+parse steps.
4. If either navigation fails visibly (error page, non-JSON), describe what you see. Otherwise, report success flags and top-level keys for both endpoints.
summary: Direct navigation confirms /api/v1/players/1 returns valid JSON (array) and /api/v2/competitions/8/seasons/2025/players/1/stats returns a JSON object, but the stats response appears to be an error wrapper with top-level keys ['title','status','detail'], so the usable stats schema is still unverified.
